openwrt_wiki.Hinweis: In general, the advice and documentation regarding WNDR3700v1 and WNDR3700v2 is also valid for WNDR3800. The only differences are with amounts of RAM and flash memory. ... There is also a WNDR3800-1CHNAS which will not respond to the normal WNDR3800 images.
openwrt_wiki.Flash Layout original: uboot 320KiB, env 128KiB, rootfs 14592KiB, config 64KiB, config_bak 64KiB, pot 64KiB, traffic_meter 64KiB, language 1024KiB, caldata 64KiB
openwrt_wiki.Opening the case: Torx (T8); two screws visible on the bottom; four more screws under the rubber feet (not glued, removable)
openwrt_wiki.Serial: Internal J1 4-pin connector; Pin1 3.3V, Pin2 TX, Pin3 RX, Pin4 GND; 3.3V serial port voltage; 115200 8N1, no flow control; Foto zeigt WNDR3700
openwrt_wiki.JTAG: Internal J3 connector, 14 pin header; key pin left-top on photo; Pin1 TRST, Pin2 GND, Pin3 TDI, Pin4 GND, Pin5 TDO, Pin6 GND, Pin7 TMS, Pin8 GND, Pin9 TCK, Pin10 GND, Pin11 RST, Pin12 NC, Pin13 NC, Pin14 3.3VDC
openwrt_wiki.Switch-Ports: Switch-Port 0 = Gehäuse '4', 1 = '3', 2 = '2', 3 = '1', 4 = 'WAN', 5 = CPU (trunk); Port 4 an eth1 der CPU
openwrt_wiki.OEM easy installation: Stock-Web-UI Administration/Firmware-Upgrade mit squashfs-factory.img; danach Telnet 192.168.1.1
openwrt_wiki.Recovery: TFTP: Reset-Knopf an der Unterseite beim Einschalten halten, nach 45-60 s auf 192.168.1.1 erreichbar, factory.img (oder Netgear-img) per tftp binary put
openwrt_wiki.Original firmware Bootlog: Linux 2.6.15, flash_size 16, memory 08000000 (128 MiB), hw_id:29763654+16+128, model_id:WNDR3800, REGION: WW, RTL8366S
openwrt_wiki.OpenWrt Bootlog (2012): SoC: Atheros AR7161 rev 2; Clocks CPU 680 MHz, DDR 340 MHz, AHB 170 MHz; Memory 126288k/131072k
openwrt_wiki.Rückweg Stock: mtd -r erase firmware, dann tftp WNDR3800.img

openwrt_git_61307544.message: The WNDR3700v2 and later have just six antennae. Four of those are printed on the circuit board and serve the 2.4GHz radio. Whereas the remaining two are special 5GHz Rayspan Patch Antennae which are directly connected to the 5GHz radio.
